ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In 2018, the first aircraft powered by an ion engine was created, which does not require fuel and emits no pollutants. The principle of the engine obtaining thrust is shown in the figure: gas entering the ionization chamber is ionized into positive ions, which then drift into a uniform electric field between electrodes A and B (with initial velocity negligible). The voltage between A and B is U, which accelerates the positive ions to form an ion beam. During the acceleration process, the engine gains a constant thrust. The number of positive ions drifting in per unit time is a constant, the mass of each ion is m, and the charge of each ion is Ze, where Z is a positive integer, and e is the elementary charge.

1. If the thrust obtained by the engine is F1, determine the number N of positive ions drifting between A and B per unit time.
2. The thrust F obtained by the engine varies when the power P consumed by accelerating the positive ion beam changes. Derive the expression for F/P.
3. To improve the energy conversion efficiency and maximize F/P, suggest three ways to increase F/P.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$N=\frac{F_{1}}{\sqrt{2Z e m U}}$
$\frac{F}{P}=\sqrt{\frac{2m}{Z e U}}$
use ions with a large mass; use ions with a small charge; and reduce the accelerating voltage

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is the ionization chamber; after gas enters from the left side, it is ionized into multiple positively charged ions; the dashed lines represent electrodes A and B, a voltage U is applied between A and B, and the positive ions accelerate to the right in the uniform electric field between the two electrodes, forming an ion beam and being emitted. In the diagram, the initial speed of the ions can be regarded as approximately 0. Then reason: Let the charge of each ion be q=Ze and the mass be m. When the ions are accelerated through voltage U, by the kinetic energy theorem there is ZeU = (1/2)mv^2, so v = sqrt(2ZeU/m). 1) If N positive ions enter the acceleration region per second, then the thrust obtained by the engine equals the rate of change of the momentum emitted per unit time, so F1 = Nmv, therefore N = F1/(mv) = F1/sqrt(2ZemU). 2) The electric power is P = NqU = NZeU, while the thrust F = Nmv, so F/P = (Nmv)/(NZeU) = mv/(ZeU) = sqrt(2m/(ZeU)). 3) From F/P = sqrt(2m/(ZeU)), it can be seen that increasing m, decreasing Z, and decreasing U can all increase F/P. Therefore the following can be adopted: use ions with larger mass; use ions with smaller charge quantity; reduce the accelerating voltage.

First describe the image: On the left side of the figure is the ionization chamber; after gas enters from the left side, it is ionized into multiple positively charged ions; the dashed lines represent electrodes A and B, a voltage U is applied between A and B, and the positive ions accelerate to the right in the uniform electric field between the two electrodes, forming an ion beam and being emitted. In the diagram, the initial speed of the ions can be regarded as approximately 0.

Then reason: Let the charge of each ion be q=Ze and the mass be m. When the ions are accelerated through voltage U, by the kinetic energy theorem there is ZeU = (1/2)mv^2, so v = sqrt(2ZeU/m).

1) If N positive ions enter the acceleration region per second, then the thrust obtained by the engine equals the rate of change of the momentum emitted per unit time, so F1 = Nmv, therefore
N = F1/(mv) = F1/sqrt(2ZemU).

2) The electric power is P = NqU = NZeU, while the thrust F = Nmv, so
F/P = (Nmv)/(NZeU) = mv/(ZeU) = sqrt(2m/(ZeU)).

3) From F/P = sqrt(2m/(ZeU)), it can be seen that increasing m, decreasing Z, and decreasing U can all increase F/P. Therefore the following can be adopted: use ions with larger mass; use ions with smaller charge quantity; reduce the accelerating voltage.
